Through these efforts the ammonia terminal operators invested in added security and safety measures over the years, including upgraded perimeter fencing and alarm systems, and a wall surrounding the storage tanks designed to completely contain a major storage tank leak. Entr has already identified a similar safety measure in this pre-FEED study, namely to install a wall around three sides of the CO storage tank area to direct any major leaks of CO south to the uninhabited 2 2 open water. As of 2019, an “Ammonia Operations Group” meets on a bi-monthly basis to discuss safety measures, new regulations and initiatives. Meetings are attended by the terminal operators as well as staff from Port Tampa Bay, Tampa fire, emergency management and police, and the U.S. Coast Guard among others. 3. It is envisioned that the T-RICH hub site will be equipped with its own perimeter security fence and separate guarded entry point, as well as utilize all of the latest technology in terms of CCTV cameras with motion sensing, infrared heat/cold detection, and other new intrusion detection and access control systems. The ammonia terminals in the port have been recognized as being a model for safety and concern for community welfare for other industries to follow, including the T-RICH CO terminal. 2 In future FEED study and engineering phases a full Emergency Response Plan will be developed following the “Tampa Bay Hazardous Materials Emergency Response Plan” template.
